text: Of everything in the book, which habit does the closing lesson single out as most worth keeping?
choices: When something surprises you, find out why — the actual mechanism, not "it works now".
Write the test before the code, so that the specification comes first.
Prefer composition to inheritance, since it keeps run-time choices open.
Measure before optimizing, since intuition about performance is unreliable.
explanation: It costs twenty minutes and it is the difference between getting steadily better and plateauing early with a collection of things that seem to work. Every measurement in the book exists because of it: the LinkedList result produced Chapter 15's cache material, the parallel counter produced Chapter 31, and Chapter 32's bubble-sort anomaly was reported rather than removed because the alternative was teaching something false.
